summary: anisotropy.py harmonic with --exposure-map took the null covariance of the weighted harmonic components as (2/N_eff) I: with a non-uniform exposure the variances of a and b are unequal and correlated, so the Rayleigh probability overstated the significance of a dipole along the less exposed axis and the amplitude upper limit was too tight.

observables: harmonic.rayleigh_probability and harmonic.sigma_per_component of anisotropy.py harmonic with --exposure-map
upper_limit.neyman_limit, upper_limit.expected_limit, upper_limit.median_isotropic_amplitude and upper_limit.upper_limit with --exposure-map
impact.bias: the null variance along the most exposure-modulated axis was understated (for a relative exposure 1 + 0.9 cos alpha, N Var(a) = 6.39 against 4.59 from N_eff), so a dipole along that axis looked more significant (20000 events, true amplitude 0.06: p = 1.7e-6 reported against 7.5e-5) and its Neyman upper limit excluded amplitudes it should not (0.100 against 0.105 at CL 0.95; the scipy CDF at the old limit is 0.089, not 0.05); along the better exposed axis the old significance was understated instead
impact.trigger: an exposure map whose relative exposure is not constant in right ascension; without a map, with a uniform map and for the solar, sidereal and anti-sidereal checks the numbers are unchanged

outputs.how_to_recognize: anisotropy.py harmonic with --exposure-map: JSON on stdout with harmonic, upper_limit, label and warnings

remedy: rerun anisotropy.py harmonic with the same events and exposure map on a release that has the fix and replace the Rayleigh probability and the upper limits; the script's JSON is not an envelope artifact, so the scan finds only computational-run records that list it as a tool, and other results that quote its numbers need a manual check
